scenes.headline: How SKY-001 plans a machine before drawing it
scenes.sub: Skyfall's engineering world model, from one image to a build plan
scenes.say: Hi, I'm Jetty! Skyfall's new model turns one picture of a machine into a plan for building it.

scenes.text: Instead of one long program, SKY-001 splits the object into a tree of parts, then draws how every part is built, many at once.
scenes.say: A language model writes one long program. This model splits the machine into a tree of parts, then draws each part's build, many at once.

steps.say: It starts from a single image of the product.
The composer decides what it is made of, one level at a time.
The construction model works out how each leaf is built.
Together: a tree, and a build sequence for every part.

items.say: First, a rough shape of the whole object.
Then it splits it into assemblies, and those again, side by side.
Then a refiner fills in what the rough shape never had.

steps.say: For one part, it first plans the solid after every step.
Between each pair of states, it draws the sketch that turns one into the next.
Each drawing is rolled out roughly first, in a compressed space.
Then a refiner adds sharp lines and exact corners.
Here is one sketch. On the left, the target outline.
In the middle, the latent rollout: the layout is right, the corners are soft.
On the right, the refined rollout, redrawn at full resolution.

scenes.title: CAD construction benchmark, IoU
scenes.say: On Skyfall's CAD benchmark, it matches GPT-6 Astra on accuracy, and reports doing it fifty-one times faster, at a hundred and fiftieth of the cost.

scenes.text: The tree shortens the wait, small latents cut the cost, and an editable CAD file is still on the roadmap.
scenes.say: The tree shortens the wait. Small latents cut the cost. But today the output is a visual plan, and an editable CAD file is still on the roadmap.

recap: Split the object into a tree
scenes.say: Split it into a tree. Plan the states, then the sketches. Rough first, detail last.
